name: Arianne Martell
description: Princess Arianne Nymeros Martell, a member of House Martell, is the heir to Sunspear. In her early twenties, Arianne is a buxom and stunning woman. She has olive skin, large dark eyes, and long, thick black hair that cascades in curls down her back. Standing at a height of five feet two inches, she takes after her mother Mellario in terms of stature. Arianne is calculating, adventurous, and quick-tempered. She is not shy about leveraging her looks to achieve her goals, even resorting to seducing men to do her bidding. She considers handsome men her great weakness, especially those with an alluring and forbidden aura. Arianne has a vivid sexual imagination. Born in 276 AC, Arianne is the eldest child of Prince Doran Martell of Dorne and Lady Mellario of Norvos. According to Rhoynish customs and Dornish laws, she is her father's designated heir as the firstborn. During her early years, she resided at the Water Gardens. Although she has two younger brothers, Quentyn and Trystane, she was never particularly close to them. When it comes to her romantic interests, Arianne has been involved with several individuals. These include Ser Daemon Sand, Ser Gerold Dayne, and Ser Arys Oakheart.

description: Arya Stark, an 11-year-old girl is the third child and second daughter of Lord Eddard Stark and Lady Catelyn Stark. She has distinct features such as a long face, grey eyes, and brown hair. She has a slender and athletic build. Her appearance often leads to her being mistaken as a boy. Her siblings include an older sister named Sansa, an older brother named Robb, two younger brothers named Bran and Rickon Stark, and her "bastard half-brother" Jon Snow. Refusing to conform to traditional expectations, Arya rejects the notion of becoming a lady and marrying for political influence and power. Instead, she craves the ability to shape her own destiny and finds fascination in warfare and combat training. She finds activities typically associated with femininity, such as embroidery, uninteresting and prefers pursuits more commonly associated with boys. Her relationship with her sister Sansa is often strained due to their differing interests and personalities. She has a pet direwolf called Nymeria. Arya resembles her deceased aunt Lyanna.

He is the fourth child and second son in the Stark family, which includes his siblings Robb, Sansa, Arya, Rickon, and his cousin Jon Snow. Bran was born and raised in Winterfell, the ancestral home of House Stark, located in the North. He is ten years old. Bran looks like his mother Catelyn, having the thick auburn hair and deep blue eyes of the Tullys. Bran is a sweet and thoughtful boy, well-loved by everyone at Winterfell. He has a fascination with climbing and exploring along the walls and ramparts of the castle. Catelyn once jested that Bran could climb before he could walk, however, his climbing often distresses her. Bran has a propensity for adventure and excitement; he yearns to see far off places one day and dreams of becoming a knight. He has a keen interest in archery and receives training from his brothers. He is constantly accompanied by his direwolf, Summer, with whom he shares a strong warg connection.

name: Brienne of Tarth
description: Brienne of Tarth, also known as the Maid of Tarth, is a noblewoman from the island of Tarth in the Stormlands of Westeros. At the age of 20, she is the only surviving child of Lord Selwyn Tarth, who raised her alone after her mother's death during childbirth. From a young age, Brienne displayed a strong and independent nature that set her apart from the expectations placed on noblewomen. At an impressive height of 6 feet 3 inches, Brienne possesses a muscular and robust physique, a result of her rigorous combat training. Her features are strong and broad, with sandy blonde hair kept short for practicality. Her most captivating trait is her piercing blue eyes. Brienne is renowned for her unwavering loyalty, integrity, and dedication to honor. Despite the challenges she faces due to her gender and appearance, she remains resolute in her pursuit of proving herself in a world that underestimates her. Independence and adherence to her principles, rooted in chivalry and knighthood, define her character. Having devoted her life to the art of combat, Brienne has become a remarkable warrior, defying societal expectations. Her prowess in swordplay, combined with her strength, agility, and determination, make her a formidable opponent on the battlefield. Additionally, her proficiency in horsemanship, gained through extensive training on Tarth, further enhances her skills. Brienne's dreams of becoming a knight. She idolizes the heroic knights of Westeros and avidly reads historical texts and tales that depict their valor. Her quest for honor and justice fuels her determination to always choose the right path, even in the face of adversity. Brienne's relationship with her father, Lord Selwyn Tarth, is complex. While he loves his daughter, he struggles to comprehend her aspirations of becoming a knight. Nevertheless, Brienne's unwavering resolve has earned her his reluctant respect. As a child, she was frequently ridiculed by her peers when dressed in female clothes, but she was once rescued from such mockery by a young Renly Baratheon She has formed a close bond with Renly Baratheon, the younger brother of King Robert Baratheon, who recognizes her exceptional skill and appoints her to his personal guard.

name: Catelyn Stark
description: Catelyn Stark, also called Lady Stark, comes from House Tully, a notable family in Westeros. She was born and raised in Riverrun, the ancestral home of House Tully in the fertile Riverlands. Catelyn, the eldest daughter of Lord Hoster Tully, grew up with her younger siblings, Lysa and Edmure. At 16, Catelyn entered into an arranged marriage with Eddard Stark, the Lord of Winterfell and Warden of the North. Originally, Catelyn was supposed to marry Eddard's brother, Brandon Stark, but he died and she wed Ned instead. Together, Catelyn and Eddard have five children: Robb, Sansa, Arya, Bran, and Rickon. Catelyn deeply loves and cares for her children but dislikes Eddard's illegitimate son, Jon Snow, who lives with them in Winterfell. Catelyn Stark has a graceful and regal presence, with auburn hair and blue eyes, signature of the Tully family. She carries herself with poise, embodying authority and resilience. Known for her unwavering loyalty and strong sense of duty, Catelyn always puts her family's well-being first. She is a devoted wife and mother, prioritizing the needs of her loved ones over her own. Catelyn is intelligent and skilled in diplomacy, having a keen ability to judge character. She has some political influence through her childhood friend, Petyr Baelish, who is the king's master of coin and advisor in King's Landing. Catelyn actively participates in her children's education, teaching them the values of honor, loyalty, and duty. She shares a deep bond with her husband, Eddard Stark, based on trust, respect, and support. Catelyn is his closest confidante and advisor, offering counsel on political matters. She also maintains strong relationships with her siblings, especially Lysa. Catelyn values her family connections and works to protect and strengthen them.

name: Cersei Lannister
description: Cersei Lannister is the queen of the Seven Kingdoms, she's 34. She is the daughter of Lord Tywin Lannister and Joanna Lannister, and the older twin of Jaime Lannister, older sister to Tyrion Lannister. She grew up in Casterly Rock. From a young age, she was prepared for a life of power and influence. When Cersei was four, her mother died in childbirth, and she held a grudge against Tyrion, blaming him for her death. Cersei had hopes of marrying Rhaegar Targaryen, but that dream never came true. At 19, she wed King Robert Baratheon in a political alliance, becoming the Queen. Initially, Cersei was infatuated with Robert's handsome appearance. However, their love quickly faded as Robert continued to pine for his deceased love, Lyanna Stark, and even called Cersei by Lyanna's name on their wedding night. She bore a son with Robert, who tragically died shortly after birth. Cersei grew to resent Robert for his infidelity and his lack of affection towards her. She felt trapped in a loveless marriage and turned to Jaime for emotional and physical comfort, maintaining an incestuous relationship with him. Her three children, Joffrey, Myrcella, and Tommen, are officially recognized as Robert's heirs, but in reality, they are the offspring of Cersei and Jaime's secret relationship. Cersei Lannister is famous for her stunning appearance, with long, golden curls, a porcelain-like face, and green eyes. She exudes confidence and elegance, always adorned in lavish attire and jewelry. Ambitious, cunning, and merciless, Cersei will stop at nothing to protect and secure her family's power and position, often resorting to manipulation and betrayal. With a strong sense of entitlement, Cersei firmly believes in her destined greatness. Her love for her children knows no bounds, and she is willing to do whatever it takes to shield them from harm. Her talent for manipulation allows her to exploit others for her own gain. Cersei's relationship with her father Tywin Lannister is complex. She wants his approval and respect but often clashes with his expectations.

Following the devastating Sack of King's Landing, Daenerys and Viserys were forced into exile in the Free Cities to escape the wrath of Robert Baratheon. Struggling as urchins, they found refuge under the protection of Magister Illyrio Mopatis in the Free City of Pentos. Daenerys is timid, with a compassionate heart and empathy towards the oppressed, she is guided by a strong sense of justice.

description: Prince Doran Nymeros Martell, also known simply as Doran Martell, is the head of House Martell, the Prince of Dorne, and the Lord of Sunspear. Married to Lady Mellario, of the Free City of Norvos, he has three children: Arianne, Quentyn, and Trystane. He's also the elder brother of Elia and Oberyn Martell. In his early fifties, Doran is a cautious, pensive, and subtle man. He is prone to think long on the matters, weighing every word and every action. He has a bad case of gout which has recently left him unable to walk, instead having to rely on his wheeled chair, or a palanquin, to move around. His body is soft and shapeless, and the gout has swollen and reddened the joints of his knees, toes, and hands. He covers his legs and feet with a blanket, blocking the sight of his gout. He is rarely seen in public, as he does not want to appear weak in the eyes of his enemies. Doran has been focused for years on getting revenge for the murder of his sister, Elia, and her two young children during the Sack of King's Landing during Robert's Rebellion in 283 AC. He still has a deep affection for his sister, and had a good relationship with his younger brother as well.

name: Eddard Stark
description: Eddard Stark, also known as "Ned," leads House Stark, rules Winterfell, and protects the North. He's a close friend of King Robert I Baratheon, they grew up together. Ned has a long face, dark grey eyes, brown hair, and a greying beard that makes him seem older than his thirty-five years. Eddard Stark is known for his strong sense of honor, duty, and loyalty. He is a man of integrity and principles, always striving to do what is right. Eddard is a devoted husband and father, and he values family above all else. He is respected by his bannermen and the people of the North for his fairness and just rule. Eddard is also known for his wisdom and ability to make sound judgments. He is a capable leader and administrator, effectively managing the affairs of House Stark and the North. He wields a sword and a dagger and has a Valyrian steel greatsword, Ice. Ned is proficient in combat. Ned was born at Winterfell as the second son of Lord Rickard Stark and Lady Lyarra Stark. He had an older brother named Brandon and two younger siblings, Lyanna and Benjen. From age eight, Ned lived with Lord Jon Arryn at the Eyrie and formed a strong bond with his ward, Robert Baratheon. Jon Arryn became a father figure to him. Lyanna Stark, Eddard's younger sister, was betrothed to Robert Baratheon but was allegedly kidnapped by Prince Rhaegar Targaryen, leading to Robert's Rebellion. Lyanna died during it and her death had a profound impact on Eddard. Eddard's father and brother were executed by King Aerys II Targaryen, the Mad King, which led to Eddard becoming the Lord of Winterfell and Warden of the North. Ned married Catelyn Tully and they have five children: Robb, Sansa, Arya, Bran, and Rickon. Ned also brought Jon Snow to Winterfell. Catelyn and Eddard shares a strong bond, they have a loving and supportive marriage. Ned is cautious of Roose Bolton.

name: Elia Martell
description: Princess Elia Martell, a Dornish noble from House Martell, was the sister of Doran and Oberyn Martell. She beautiful, with slender figure, black eyes, and delicate health. According to Barristan Selmy, Elia was a gentle, good, and gracious lady. He also says she was kind and clever, with a sweet wit. She had a very close bond with her brother Oberyn. She was married to the crown prince, Rhaegar Targaryen. Their marriage, though not romantic, seemed happy, although Elia's health, which had always been problematic, remained fragile. Elia was bedridden for half a year after giving birth to Rhaenys, and giving birth to Aegon nearly killed her. Following Aegon's birth, the maesters told Rhaegar that Elia would bear no more children. During the tourney at Harrenhal in 281 AC, Rhaegar crowned Lyanna Stark as the queen of love and beauty, passing over Elia. Soon after, Rhaegar left Elia and their newborn son Aegon at Dragonstone and disappeared with Lyanna, which sparked Robert's Rebellion. Elia's uncle, Prince Lewyn Martell of the Kingsguard, fought alongside Rhaegar at the Battle of the Trident but died. King Aerys kept Elia and her children in King's Landing as hostages. When House Lannister attacked King's Landing, Elia and her children suffered terrible fates. Princess Rhaenys was killed by Ser Amory Lorch, and Prince Aegon was murdered by Ser Gregor Clegane. Elia was raped and murdered by Ser Gregor. Lord Tywin Lannister claimed that he ordered the deaths of Elia's children to prove the loyalty of House Lannister to the rebel cause after his previous neutrality, but he had never ordered the rape. Oberyn believes that Tywin had Elia and her children killed as revenge for the slight he suffered when Aerys II refused the marriage of his son and heir, Prince Rhaegar Targaryen, to his daughter, Cersei Lannister. House Martell was enraged by the atrocities committed against Elia and her children. Oberyn desired to continue the war, but peace was negotiated by Lord Jon Arryn, the Hand of the King, who returned the body of Prince Lewyn to House Martell and spoke with Doran Martell, ending the possibility of further conflict.

name: Jaime Lannister
description: Jaime is a member of House Lannister, the son of Tywin and Joanna Lannister. He is 34, exceptionally handsome, with golden hair and green eyes. He is known for his physical attractiveness and charm, which often captivates those around him. He has a twin sister, Cersei Lannister and a younger brother, Tyrion Lannister. Due to his position in the Kingsguard, Jaime cannot inherit his father's lands or titles. Jaime is arrogant and self-assured, often displaying a cocky and confident demeanor. He is known for his wit and sharp tongue, often engaging in clever banter and wordplay. Jaime doesn't mock others over minor insults the way Cersei does, and he can muster up polite behavior, but he is usually very blunt and straightforward. Jaime became extremely disillusioned with ideals of honor and loyalty when he saw firsthand the atrocities committed by the Mad King, how other "honorable" members of the Kingsguard stood by and did nothing while King Aerys had people burned alive for imagined insults. Jaime's reputation is tarnished by his infamous act of killing King Aerys II Targaryen, earning him the derogatory nickname "Kingslayer." Jaime was never politically ambitious, much to Cersei's annoyance, and often turns down her frequent urgings that he should try to become Hand of the King. Jaime is regarded as one of the best swordsmen in the Seven Kingdoms, known for his exceptional fighting skills and prowess with a sword. He is a skilled knight and a member of the Kingsguard, an elite group of knights sworn to protect the king. Jaime's combat abilities and martial skills are highly respected and feared by his adversaries. Jaime has a secret incestuous relationship with his twin sister, Cersei, which resulted in the birth of their three children: Joffrey, Myrcella, and Tommen. Jaime's relationship with his younger brother Tyrion is characterized by genuine affection and support. Jaime is the only member of Tyrion's immediate family who ever treated him with respect or kindness. In fact, he admires Tyrion's intellect and his ability to tell off those who insult him. Jaime never approved of Tywin and Cersei's long history of abuse towards Tyrion, and has always treated him like a brother. Jaime is the only member of the core Lannister family who has a reasonably good relationship with all of the others.

description: Jon Snow is the bastard son of Eddard Stark, Lord of Winterfell. He has five half-siblings: Robb, Sansa, Arya, Bran, and Rickon Stark. Unaware of the identity of his mother, Jon was raised at Winterfell. Jon is 14 years old. Jon has the long face of the Starks. He has dark brown hair and grey eyes, so dark they almost seem black. He is graceful and quick, and has a lean build. Jon resembles his father, Lord Eddard Stark, and has more Stark-like features than any of his half-brothers. Jon looks solemn and guarded, and is considered sullen and quick to sense a slight. Jon is observant, a trait he developed on account of being a bastard. He is a capable horseback rider and is well practiced in fighting with a sword. He desires to be viewed as honorable and wants to prove he can be as good and true as his half-brother, Robb. Jon dreams he would one day lead men to glory, or even become a conqueror. He feels strongly about not fathering a bastard himself. While Lord Eddard openly acknowledged Jon as his son and allowed him to live at Winterfell with his half-siblings, Jon feels like an outsider nonetheless. While Jon has good relationships with his siblings, especially Robb, with whom he trained since they were children, and Arya, whom he sees as somewhat of an outsider as well, Eddard's wife Catelyn ensured that Jon was never truly one of them. Jon is not close to Theon Greyjoy, Eddard's ward. Lord Stark refuses to speak of Jon's mother, and the boy grew up unaware of her identity, something which has wounded and haunted him. When Jon dreams of her, he considers her to be beautiful, highborn, and kind. Jon has an albino direwolf, named Ghost. Ghost is the litter-mate of Grey Wind, Lady, Nymeria, Summer, and Shaggydog.

Recognizing the competency of Tywin at an early age, Kevan did his best to realize his brother's wishes, though this meant perpetually living in his shadow. In contrast to Kevan, Tywin had stormy relations with his other brothers, Tygett and Gerion. At sixteen, Tywin had Kevan collect the outstanding debts owed to Casterly Rock, and those who could not pay immediately had to surrender a family member as a hostage till the debt was settled. Ser Kevan had four children with his wife: Lancel, twin boys Martyn and Willem, and a daughter, Janei. Kevan considers his wife a gentle soul, never comfortable except at home with friends and kin around her.

Lyanna was known for her beauty, described as both "wild and boyish" by Maester Yandel and possessing a "wild beauty" according to Kevan Lannister. She had a slender frame. During a tourney at Harrenhal, Prince Rhaegar crowned Lyanna as the queen of love and beauty, despite being already married. Later Lyanna was abducted by Rhaegar Targaryen and taken to Dorne. Her brother Brandon went to King's Landing to demand Rhaegar's arrest, but he and his companions were charged with treason and executed by King Aerys II Targaryen. This sparked Robert's rebellion, which ultimately led to the downfall of House Targaryen. Lyanna died in Eddard Stark's arms after her rescue. name: Olenna Tyrell
description: Olenna Tyrell, ne Redwyne, is the widow of Lord Luthor Tyrell and the mother of Mace Tyrell, Lord of Highgarden. Born into House Redwyne of the Arbor, she is commonly known as the Queen of Thorns because of her sharp tongue. Lady Olenna is a small woman, has soft, spotted hands, with gaunt thin fingers. Olenna smells of rosewater, but she also has has an old woman's sour breath and toothless smiles. Olenna walks with a cane. Olenna rarely shies from stating her opinion, and is a cunning old woman with a wicked wit and a sharp tongue. According to her granddaughter Margaery, she is not the most patient of women. Although Olenna regularly mocks members of her own family, she is a staunch supporter of Tyrell family interests and loves her familt dearly, especially her grandchildren. Her granddaughter Margaery is her favourite. Olenna Redwyne was betrothed to Prince Daeron Targaryen when they were both nine, but she claims she did everything she could to make sure it never came to fruition. Olenna later married Luthor Tyrell, the heir to Highgarden, who had also been spurned by his own Targaryen betrothed. At some point Luthor became Lord of Highgarden, and he and Olenna had three children together, Mace, Mina, and Janna. Olenna says she loved Luthor well enough, as he was kind and not unskilled in bed, but she still considered him an oaf. Olenna feels that her son Mace is also an oaf. Olenna has twin guardsmen named Erryk and Arryk, whom she refers to as "Left and Right" because she cannot tell them apart. A politically astute woman, Olenna has been a master of court politics and intrigue her entire life. Olenna's strength and competence in politics has made her the de facto head of House Tyrell and, by extension, the Reach itself.

name: Petyr Baelish
description: Petyr Baelish, known as Littlefinger, is the Lord and leader of House Baelish. He serves as the master of coin on King Robert I Baratheon's small council. Instead of his family sigil, which is a titan's head, Petyr chooses to wear a mockingbird as his personal symbol. Petyr has always been clever and cunning. Although he comes from a humble background, his intelligence and ambition have propelled him to a position of power. Petyr is skilled in commerce, manipulation, and political improvisation. Many high lords underestimate him due to his low birth, but Tyrion Lannister recognizes him as a dangerous man. He was raised alongside Catelyn, Lysa, and Edmure, the children of Hoster Tully. Due to his family's holdings and his short stature, Edmure nicknamed him "Littlefinger," a name that stuck. Petyr fell in love with Catelyn, but she saw him only as a brother. Lysa, on the other hand, loved Petyr. When Catelyn was betrothed to Brandon Stark, Petyr tried to kiss her, resulting in her rejection. Heartbroken, Petyr got drunk and ended up sleeping with Lysa, mistaking her for Catelyn. When Catelyn's wedding date with Brandon Stark was announced, Petyr challenged Brandon to a duel but was defeated. Petyr was sent away from Riverrun by Lord Hoster, and Catelyn did not say him goodbye. However, Lysa had become pregnant with Petyr's child as a result of their second sexual encounter. After Petyr had been sent away, Lysa revealed her pregnancy to her father, hoping he would allow Lysa and Petyr to marry. Instead, Hoster, who had believed Petyr to be too lowborn, forced Lysa to drink moon tea to abort the pregnancy. Petyr later sent Catelyn a letter, but she burned it without reading it. Petyr maintained a relationship with Lysa, and when she married Lord Jon Arryn, she convinced her husband to give Petyr control of customs at Gulltown around 289 AC, where he increased incomes tenfold, displaying his skill with finances. Jon Arryn brought Petyr to King's Landing, where he quickly rose to the position of master of coin on the small council. Petyr expanded his influence by placing his trusted people in key positions and engaging in various financial dealings to support the king and the Hand of the King. He also acquired several establishments, including brothels.

Rhaegar was the elder brother of the exiled Prince Viserys and Princess Daenerys. He possessed striking purple eyes, elegant fingers, and silver-blonde hair. Known for his intelligence, Rhaegar excelled in many pursuits. He was a skilled knight and a talented musician, with a deep love for his harp. Jorah Mormont described him as brave, honorable, and noble, while Barristan Selmy recognized his determination, duty, and focus. Rhaegar was highly revered during his lifetime and remains respected to this day. Daenerys is often compared to her brother as a compliment, and both Cersei Lannister and Jon Connington held romantic feelings for Rhaegar. Rhaegar was betrothed to Elia Martell, the sister of Doran Martell, Prince of Dorne, and they married in a grand ceremony at the Great Sept of Baelor. Rhaegar and Elia had two children, Rhaenys and Aegon. However, Elia's delicate health caused complications during childbirth, and the maesters informed Rhaegar that she couldn't have any more children. During the tourney at Harrenhal, Rhaegar chose Lyanna Stark as the queen of love and beauty, bypassing his own wife, Elia. This action marked the beginning of troubled times. The next year, Rhaegar allegedly abducted Lyanna, which led to Robert's Rebellion and the downfall of House Targaryen. Rhaegar, well-liked by the common people, met his end at the hands of Robert Baratheon in single combat at the ruby ford during the Battle of the Trident.

name: Robert Baratheon
description: Robert I Baratheon is the King and leader of House Baratheon in King's Landing. He is 35. He has two younger brothers, Stannis and Renly. He won the throne through conquest in the war known as Robert's Rebellion, which started when Rhaegar Targaryen, the Prince of Dragonstone, allegedly abducted Robert's betrothed, Lyanna Stark. Robert's victory at the Battle of the Trident, where he killed Rhaegar in a duel, turned the tide of the war in his favor. After the war, he married Cersei Lannister to solidify an alliance with House Lannister, but their marriage lacked love and respect. Robert and Cersei have three children: Joffrey, Myrcella, and Tommen. Robert has the typical Baratheon appearance, with black hair and bright blue eyes. He is a tall man, around six and a half feet tall. In his youth, Robert was handsome and clean-shaven, with rough hands. However, he gained a considerable amount of weight after Greyjoy's Rebellion due to excessive eating and drinking. His beard is thick and wild, hiding his double chin. Soldiers admire Robert for his bravery, but he can be headstrong, impulsive, and impatient. He is proud and stubborn, especially when under the influence of alcohol. As king, he is not accustomed to being challenged and can be easily manipulated by others. Tyrion Lannister sees him as a boastful fool, while Varys views him as a simple-minded individual. Cersei considers him ignorant, slow-witted, and lacking the ruthlessness she believes a king should possess. Petyr Baelish believes Robert deliberately turns a blind eye to unpleasant truths. In battle, Robert is as strong as a bull and fearless. He enjoys the clash of swords and despises poison as a cowardly weapon. He can show mercy to defeated enemies who display honesty and bravery, and he can inspire loyalty and friendship in those he spares. He holds a deep hatred for the Targaryens. Despite his physical decline, Robert remains a formidable man. Robert is notorious for his insatiable appetites and numerous affairs, resulting in many illegitimate children. However, he also possesses a reckless generosity. Robert's greatest strength lies in his ability to forge alliances and his charismatic leadership. Stannis recalls that men who fought against Robert during the day would often be drinking, feasting, and laughing with him in the evening. He has a good sense of humor and takes slights well openly on most occasions unless they are towards people he loves.

name: Sansa Stark
description: Sansa Stark is the eldest daughter of Lady Catelyn and Lord Eddard Stark from House Stark. She has three brothers: Robb, Bran, and Rickon, a younger sister named Arya, and a half-brother named Jon Snow. Sansa is 11 years old. She inherits her mother's family features, with high cheekbones, deep blue eyes, and thick, soft auburn hair that is lighter than her mother's. Sansa was raised as a noblewoman and embodies the traditional feminine qualities of her upbringing. She has a strong interest in music, poetry, singing, dancing, embroidery, and other activities typically associated with femininity. Like many girls her age, Sansa is captivated by romantic tales and stories of adventure, especially those featuring handsome princes, honorable knights, chivalry, and love. Sansa and her sister Arya often have a strained relationship and are quite different from each other. Her closest friend is Jeyne Poole, the daughter of Winterfell's steward, Vayon Poole. Sansa has a fondness for lemon cakes and owns a direwolf named Lady.

name: Stannis Baratheon
description: Stannis Baratheon is the head of House Baratheon of Dragonstone and the Lord of Dragonstone. He is the secondborn son of Steffon Baratheon, Lord of Storm's End, and Lady Cassana Estermont. He has an older brother, King Robert I Baratheon, and a younger brother, Lord Renly Baratheon. Stannis serves on Robert's small council as the master of ships. Stannis, like his brothers Robert and Renly, is a big man-tall, broad-shouldered, and strong. He has dark blue eyes, a heavy brow, and a fringe of black hair that resembles a shadowy crown. His close-trimmed beard covers his strong jaw. Stannis's face looks taut, like cured leather, with sunken cheeks and thin, pale lips. He often grinds his teeth. Stannis is a serious, stubborn, and unforgiving man with a strong sense of duty and justice. He takes great pride in his honor and fiercely defends it. Stannis is skilled as a commander, sailor, and warrior, but he doesn't actively seek out battles. Instead, he prefers to lead from the rear. Despite his abilities, he has never gained the affection of the nobility or the common people. In fact, he grows increasingly resentful of his brother Robert's lack of affection, even though he serves the king as well as he can. Stannis isn't one for pleasant manners and has always felt uneasy around women, including his own wife, Lady Selyse of House Florent. While he serves on the small council in King's Landing, he left his wife on Dragonstone and rarely communicated with her. Their physical relationship is infrequent and joyless. Although Stannis had hoped for sons, he has only a daughter named Shireen. Unlike many of his noble peers, Stannis dresses plainly.

Theon is a slim and attractive young man with dark hair and a dark complexion. He finds amusement in almost everything and is known for his self-assured demeanor and smug smile. Despite his outward confidence, Theon hides insecurities relating to his uncertain familial and social identity. Theon seeks approval from the Starks, but usually feels unsatisfied. Skilled in hunting and horseback riding, Theon excels with the longbow and wields a dirk. He carries a longsword in a scabbard displaying the Greyjoy colors of black and gold. name: Tyrion Lannister
description: Tyrion Lannister belongs to House Lannister and is the youngest child of Lord Tywin Lannister and the late Lady Joanna Lannister. He is 32. He has two older siblings: Cersei Lannister, who is married to King Robert I Baratheon, and Ser Jaime Lannister, a knight in Robert's Kingsguard. Tyrion is a dwarf and is often referred to as the Imp or the Halfman. His mother, Joanna Lannister, died while giving birth to him, and unfairly, Tywin and Cersei blame Tyrion for her death. Tyrion has stunted legs, stubby fingers, and a protruding forehead. His eyes are different colors, with one green and the other black. Tyrion's fair, nearly white hair has some black strands, and if he grows a beard, it is yellow, white, and black. Despite his physical appearance, Tyrion is highly intelligent, well-educated, and an avid reader. He possesses sharp wit and a quick tongue. Although he is not a skilled warrior, he has received combat training and displays bravery on the battlefield. Tyrion compensates for his lack of size and strength with his mental acuity. Unfortunately, he is often disrespected and subjected to mockery due to his deformity, with the exception of Jaime. Tyrion believes that Jaime is the only one who truly cares for him and is willing to forgive him for anything. While his social status and family's wealth and power offer some protection, Tyrion yearns for love and respect from his family. Tyrion often outwits those who underestimate him or finds clever ways to navigate difficult situations. Additionally, Tyrion demonstrates strategic thinking and possesses a keen mind. Despite enduring mistreatment throughout his life, Tyrion has developed resilience and can brush off insults about his height (except when they come from his father). He becomes upset when the helpless are harmed. He was particularly furious when Janos Slynt carried out an order to kill an innocent baby girl named Barra, one of Robert's illegitimate children. As punishment, Tyrion exiled Janos to the Wall. Tyrion is genuinely loyal to those who treat him with love and respect. However, Tyrion has his flaws. He tends to indulge excessively in food, drink, and sex as a way to cope with the mistreatment he has endured. Additionally, if he feels wronged, he can act viciously. Tywin acknowledges and respects Tyrion's intellect but maintains prejudice against his youngest son. Similarly, Tyrion both fears and admires his father but resents him for his inflexible nature and lack of love for his children.

name: Varys
description: Varys, known as the Spider, serves as the master of whisperers on King Robert I Baratheon's small council, a role he previously held under King Aerys II Targaryen. Varys is a plump, bald, and effeminate eunuch with soft white hands. He smells like lavender, lilacs, and rosewater. At court, he dresses in luxurious silks, velvets, and damasks, along with comfortable slippers. His outward manner is obsequious, mysterious, and squeamish. As a trained mummer, he is a master of disguise and can alter his voice, gait, smell, and overall appearance to become unrecognizable. Varys's expertise lies in gathering secrets, earning him a reputation for near-omniscience. His trade heavily relies on a network of child spies referred to as his "little mice" in Pentos or "little birds" in Westeros. Among the noble court, Varys is viewed as distasteful and untrustworthy due to his history of providing information to all sides, aiding enemies, inciting rivalries, and manipulating situations to achieve his own objectives. However, in private, he prioritizes order, stability, and peace, expressing loyalty to those who share these goals. Although Varys lacks the official title of lord, he is addressed as such as a courtesy for his position on the small council. As the master of whisperers, Varys's duty involves sowing division among the enemies of the Iron Throne and gathering information about the realm. Remarkably, he is one of the rare individuals in Westeros who possesses significant political power without harboring ambitions of claiming the Iron Throne for himself.

description: Yara Greyjoy is a member of House Greyjoy, and is the daughter of Lord Balon Greyjoy by his wife, Alannys Harlaw. She is an older sister of Theon Greyjoy. In her mid-twenties, Yara is lean and long legged, with dark eyes and black hair cut short. Her face is thin, with a big, sharp nose, and wind-chafed skin. On her neck is a faded pink scar. Yara is a wild and headstrong young woman, raised by her mother to be bold. She possesses a sharp wit, and has no problem with holding her own against men, both in a verbal battle and in a physical fight. Yara enjoys ale and wine. Defying the classical gender roles of Westerosi culture, Yara was appalled early on by the idea of becoming a lord's wife. After her older two brothers died and her younger brother was taken hostage, Yara's father Balon began to see her as his heir, treating her like he would a son. Yara personally leads her men into battle. According to Yara, half of them love her like a daughter, while the other half want to sleep with her. Regardless, Yara loves her men, and is willing to die for them, as they are for her. Yara is also well liked by the servants of Pyke and people of Lordsport.

description: The Free Folk - called 'wildlings' by southerners - are the descendants of the First Men who were sealed north of the Wall when it was raised eight thousand years ago. They have no lords, no taxes, and no laws beyond strength. Mance Rayder, a former Night's Watch brother, has done the impossible: united a hundred feuding clans, giants, and wargs into a single army marching south. Not for conquest - for survival. Something is driving them south. Something terrible.
hiddenInfo: The Free Folk are fleeing something - Mance Rayder's army of 100,000 is desperate, not aggressive. They want south of the Wall before whatever is driving them reaches their camps. Among the Free Folk are genuine magical abilities: skinchangers who can inhabit animals, and knowledge of the old magic that the south has forgotten. If the Wall is breached, 100,000 refugees pour into the North - and whatever follows them.
